messages:
taylor_sales: Heads-up: MedCore wants a 2-week POC next Wed to run inference from their VPC. They asked which connectivity option is fastest to stand up and which preserves original client IPs for downstream auth and auditing. Also asked for an estimated incremental cost for the POC. @ashley_netops @leah_security @nate_engineer

ashley_netops: Fastest: PrivateLink (interface endpoint). No route table changes, works across accounts. Setup timeline: ~1 business day once we have their endpoint subnet + SG. Peering needs approvals and route changes; could take 2-3 days.

leah_security: Important: PrivateLink terminates at the customer's ENI and we see traffic from the VPC endpoint. If they need per-request client IPs for security logs, we can inject X-Forwarded-For headers at our edge proxy. If they insist on seeing original TCP source IPs on our backend, VPC peering (or a transit arrangement) keeps the source IP intact. Clarify what "preserve IP" means for them.

nate_engineer: Additional technical tradeoffs: with PrivateLink we place an NLB in our account and publish a service name. TLS: if they do TLS inspection we recommend mutual TLS or providing cert chain to avoid MITM failures. For perf, both options are fine for POC volumes.

ashley_netops: Ops checklist for customer (PrivateLink):
- Provide VPC ID and subnet(s) for endpoint ENIs
- Add outbound SG rule: TCP 443 -> Redwood endpoint ENI CIDR
- Open egress to our NLB port(s) and ask if TLS inspection is present
For peering:
- Confirm no CIDR overlap
- Create peering request and accept on our side
- Update route tables + SGs to allow peered CIDRs

leah_security: Security questionnaire bits to collect now:
- Do you require mutual TLS? Y/N
- Will your egress traffic be inspected by TLS proxy? Y/N
- Do you require customer-managed KMS for logs? Y/N
- Which compliance reports do you need (SOC2, ISO)?

taylor_sales: Pricing question from MedCore: "How much extra will PrivateLink cost for a 2-week POC vs peering?"

ashley_netops: Ballpark (region-dependent):
- PrivateLink: endpoint ~$0.01/hr per interface (~$7/week per AZ) + data processing ~$0.01-0.02/GB. If they create 2 endpoints for HA, double the interface hourly.
- Peering: no endpoint hourly. Cross-account VPC data transfer pricing applies (roughly $0.01/GB between AZs/accounts), and some ops time.
For a low-traffic POC (<100GB total) cost delta is usually <$50. Use PrivateLink to reduce ops friction.

nate_engineer: Quick validation commands for their team once endpoint exists:
```
# basic API test from their bastion
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" https://internal-api.redwood.example/v1/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
# TLS testing when inspection suspected (pin cert or use --cacert)
curl --resolve "internal-api.redwood.example:443:10.2.4.5" --cacert /tmp/redwood-ca.pem https://internal-api.redwood.example/
```
Also check DNS resolution and ensure endpoint-private-dns is enabled if they want hostname routing.

deploy-bot: Notice: service offer 'pl-svc-9d8f7a' created in redwood-prod. NLB subnets: 10.100.12.0/24, 10.100.13.0/24.

leah_security: For our security handoff doc: we'll provide a sample SG snippet and a one-page checklist for their SecOps. Sample SG snippet:
```
# Example customer outbound SG for PrivateLink
Type: HTTPS  Protocol: TCP  Port: 443  Destination: 10.2.4.0/24  Description: Allow outbound to Redwood Interface Endpoint ENIs
```
Also include instructions for capturing X-Forwarded-For and enabling request-id headers.

taylor_sales: Action items: 1) I'll ask MedCore whether they need TCP-level source-ip or header-level client IP. 2) Ashley to DM the PL service name + NLB subnet CIDRs and hourly estimates. 3) Leah to attach the security checklist + sample SG to the RFP answer. 4) Nate to prepare a one-click curl script for their engineers.

ashley_netops: Will send service name + rough cost calc. If they want mutual TLS we can stand up mTLS certs but that adds time.

nate_engineer: I'll bundle the smoke tests and sample curl into a small script and put it in the POC zip.

taylor_sales: Thanks all. I'll push this to MedCore now and try to get the endpoint subnet before EOD. :rocket:
